steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Place mustard in a shallow dish or bowl; place onions in a second shallow dish or bowl. Dredge chicken in mustard to coat both sides, then dredge in onions. Place coated chicken in a lightly greased 9x13-inch baking dish.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and juices run clear.

raw_recipe.headline: Mustard Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Chicken dredged in yellow mustard and french-fried onions is about as simple and tasty as can be. Try some of the gourmet mustards for variety.
raw_recipe.name: Mustard Chicken

review.reviewBody: yum!! i have a recipe very similar to this and it is FANTASTIC & has been requested by many! in mine, you use 1/4 c "sweet & tangy" honey mustard (good for a dipping sauce too!), and a lot more french-fried onions - i got a big can and used about 2/3 of it - you smash the onion rings up as much as you can so they'll stick better. i cut my chicken breasts into 3-4 pieces each, just b/c i don't like big thick pieces of chicken. i baked at 400 for 25 mins. it is so delicious-looking & tasting! so crispy! i also found that getting it dipped/coated then refrigerating it for a 1/2 hour or so makes the coating stick better when finished. it ties with chicken marsala I (on this site) as the best chicken dish i've ever made!

REALLY yummy! Hard to believe something so simple could be so great!~ I mixed Guldens Spicy with Emerils Dijon. I also put them in the oven on a cookie cooling rack over a broiler pan. Good crunch to it..... Perfect!

EASY EASY EASY and DELICIOUS too! Followed recipe ...except that as suggested by others, I seasoned the chicken first (i used Cajun seasoning). I used half sweet mustard and half plain yellow. I crushed fried onions... As others mentioned, the fried onions on the bottom get soggy. (The only reason i am rating it 4 instead of 5 stars) I think next time, i will only dip the top of the chicken in the fried onions. (SEE MY ADDITIONAL COMMENTS AT BOTTOM OF REVIEW) Three ingredients...and couldn’t be more simple -I will definitely be making this again. ***Editing this to add that I've made this many times. Flipping the chicken half way thru baking helps to crisp the underside onions. ****Just discovered a better way.....I sprayed a cooling rack with Pam. Then put my coated chicken on it ....then put on a cookie sheet to prevent spills ....baked in the oven...worked perfectly to cook the fried onions on bottom as well as the top. Changing my review to 5 star. Easy and delicious. I can also recommend garlic pepper fried onions ...if you can't find....and garlic powder and black pepper to the onions for an additional yummy flavor.

I didn't think my 16 yr old son was going to like it because he HATES onions, so I just told him I made a new chicken recipe that was a little spicy and kind of like fried chicken but it was baked. He was like "huh?" and I just told him he'd have to wait and see. Both my husband & son LOVED it. The only change I made to the recipe was the kind of mustard I used. Kroger grocery stores have one called Sweet Hot Mustard. I put the chicken in a gallon sized bag, squirted the mustard in and let it marinate for a couple hours. Then I put the fried onions into a bowl, coated them and put them on a broiling pan and baked. I lowered the temp to 350 because the fried onions were starting to get too dark but even so, it turned out delicious!

Just loved this recipe. I have done this before and it has alway been a hit. The only change I made was just bonelss chicken legs and breast then I did the following. In my roasting pan I spread out 1 cup of long grain rice. I placed the Mustard Chicken on top and carefully added 2 cups of water. Covered and baked in a 350 oven for about 1 hour. The flavours from the recipe was absorbed by the rice. Work great.

This is my favorite chicken recipe. I use half dijon and half honey mustard. I add bread crumbs and finely grated parmesan to the fried onions. I bake it on a rack but it doesn't crisp up like I'd like so I'd be interested any suggestions. Still VERY tasty.

For those that thought it turned out dry, the recommended cooking time of appox 55 min is way too long. Pounded to an even thickness and baked 40 min leaves this chicken very moist. Just use your favorite mustard and a little garlic pwr and you have a real tasty meal. Cooking any boneless skinless chicken has a small margin of error before it is over cooked.

This was very good. I used the suggestions of others and put the paprika, garlic salt and salt on one side. I used Honey Mustard. I didn't have any problems with getting the fried onions to stick. After I pounded the chicken breasts I put them in a zip lock bag and poured the mustard in and let them sit for about 15 minutes. I then put the fried onions in a different zip lock bag to crush them. Poured the crushed fried onions in a pie dish and then put the mustard covered chicken in the pie dish to coat. Came out beautifully. Because I only used 2 breasts that were pounded, I only had to cook them for 40 minutes and they came out done and juicy! This is definately on my rotation and will be trying it out with different mustards. Thanks for sharing the recipe!! :)

I am very stingy with my stars, but this deserves the top! As another reviewer suggested, I used honey-mustard mixed with regular mustard, and glad I did, as it gave a nice sweet flavor, but not over-powering. First I pounded the chicken breasts to an even thickness. Used the food processor to finely crush the french-fried onion rings, but I will warn you that the large can of rings will only coat just over two chicken breasts. Perhaps it's because I pounded them out, so more meat to coat, but it SO helps to cook them evenly, and they don't need to cook as long, so are more juicy and tender. Truly an excellent flavor; my son-in-law asked me to give the recipe to HIS mother; the highest compliment out there, I think!

I made this last night for 3 fussy eaters! Wow! They really liked it! It was time for a change with the "chicken." We took a few other suggestions, mixed a few different mustards and I even added a honey mustard mayo! I mixed panko and ff onions together! Very good! Pounded the chicken, baked on a broil pan w/ foil @ 350 for just about 25 minutes! A keeper for sure! Very moist and crunchy, too! I also added a canadian chicken seasoning! Clean up was a breeze! Thanks!

I cut the chicken into "strips" and did them with BBQ instead of mustard. I also mixed some bread crumbs, paprika, and garlic powder in with the fried onions! In addition to the chicken strips, I did two full breasts with a sweet and spicy mustard that were also very good. Baked at 400 for 25-30 minutes. So quick and easy!

Next time I think I'd bake them on a rack like someone suggested so the breasts might crisp all around instead of just on top. My husband also thought that pounding out the chicken to make it flatter and using them, breaded, on a sandwich sounds good, as well!
I'll be making this again. The mustard makes the chicken more flavorful and keeps it moist, yet crispy. It's very easy to make too!

We love this recipe so much we've done it with pork chops too. We use spicy brown or garlic aoli mustard. Can also use some fried jalepenos with the fried onions for a little spice. Great easy and tasty recipe!
This was not good. Will not make again. The oven temp burns the onion pieces and ruined my veggie dish because I had to change everything around. That, and it just isn't good.
I thought the combination sounded so good. The chicken was tender, but I was not happy with the end product. Will not be making it again.
Very Flavorful..used 1/3 nance' s sharp 'n' creamy mustard to kick it up a notch...BAM!
I made this YEARS ago and never left a review until now.My family likes this chicken for a quick meal.Very tasty .

I end up using more mustard and fried onions because I love how it comes out with the onions & mustard on the bottom of the chicken. It's such a lovely crispy, goopy concoction. I also use Dijon mustard for an added kick. My husband requests this every time I ask him what he wants for dinner.
Yum! Made exactly as recommended and it baked up perfectly. Great with a pilaf and broccoli!
Husband didn't like mustard but now he goes crazy when I make this. Maybe it's the onions on top. ;-)
